title: PARI class-group Phase-0 reproducible fixtures
objective: Create a durable clean-build Phase-0 fixture/replay orchestrator for the integrated PARI class-group cubic and quartic gates

oracles: PARI 2.17.4 pinned source and existing stage checkers

handoff.summary: Added a durable append-only Phase-0 replay orchestrator for the existing PARI 2.17.4 analytic, splitting, prepared-cubic, and resumable-quartic checkers. Every checker-created temporary path is rooted beneath a caller-supplied artifact directory; atomic receipts hash commands, repository and checker identities, dependency receipts, PARI source/library identities, and declared outputs. A real pinned-PARI cubic-driver production, resume, independent verification, and corruption rejection all passed. Expensive splitting and quartic native matrices are named resumable stages and were intentionally not rerun by this implementation lane.
risks: The existing compiler still writes its content-addressed build cache beside mathematical sources. Durable replay snapshots the splitting baseline into the artifact root and hashes declared artifacts, but this harness does not redesign global native-cache placement.
Quartic continuation uses an attempt-local, hash-recorded launcher to replace the historical checker’s single embedded scratch PARI path. It fails closed if that exact source shape changes.
The GMP quartic replay needs about 2 GiB resident memory and a long native compile; only its orchestration and resource limits were reviewed here, not freshly executed.
next_steps: Run the default pipeline on the integration host from a clean commit and retain the resulting artifact root as the canonical Phase-0 receipt.
Run quartic-retry-javascript and quartic-retry-gmp separately so a failed expensive backend never invalidates already completed producer stages.
After integration, execute the unchanged full native gate once for the combined checkpoint; this documentation/harness-only lane did not repeat that roughly thirteen-minute suite.
